P1.reason: B separates drop mechanics, board update, lines and ending, turn order and roles; A lumps the whole game into one undifferentiated group.

differences.reason: Hurts: one group of everything names no rule at all.
Helps: counters falling into cells and the empty starting board form a coherent board-update rule.
Helps: winning lines, game end and goals together, though the diagonal line statements sit elsewhere.
Helps: legal drops and landing in the lowest empty cell is the core drop rule.
Mixed: column adjacency plus row and diagonal lines; splits line detection away from B2 awkwardly.
Helps: alternating control with red first is a clean turn-order rule.
Helps: the two players as their own small group.
